description: Jan Evertsenstraat 139-149 odd and 146-156 even, west of the Mercatorplein (1926-27): brown brick, two storeys of three two-light casements over a residential ground (paired doors), a white-painted continuous window band as the top storey (white piers between five lights), a white band at the ground-storey top, under a pitched tiled roof

tile-roof.note: the pitched tiled roof rising from the white band (12.6-15.0 m on 141); the roof itself is 3DBAG's

paired-doors.note: 141, 148: a pair of house doors at one end, windows beside them

rhythm.bays: 3 axes on the brick storeys, 5 lights in the white top band
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: doors + windows | 1-2: 3 | 3: 5 in the white band
rhythm.roofline: white band storey under a pitched tile roof
schemaLimits: the white attic band is painted timber; drawn as white painted bands and piers over brick
the brick balcony band over the ground storey is drawn as plain wall (its white edge is not drawn)

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-12-06, ruler crop of 141: white line at the ground-storey top 3.15-3.4 m, windows 4.0-5.3 and 7.25-8.85 m, white band 9.6-12.6 m with lights 10.9-12.3 m between white piers, tiles 12.6-15.0 m; storeys 3.2/3.1/3.2/3.0 m; palette-from-strip band rows 9.45-9.55, 10.55-11.85, 12.47-12.5 m
strip.jpg 2024-12-06: 148, white band rows 10.75-11.85 m, the same body
strip.jpg 2024-12-06: 154, the same body (tree over the uppers on 152/158)
palette over the type's 12 pands (de-baarsjes-palettes.ts): wall #5a4c39, frames #abac96, white band #b2b39c (151275's band median, n=2 type-wide #b8b9a7)

schemaLimits: brick balcony band over the ground storey
